title: Flat wizard cannot capture a flat when a filter move is needed - its wheel move neither takes effect nor is confirmed, while the same move works from Equipment
what_happened: Every Quick Capture run that needs a wheel move dies with 'filter wheel did not confirm position 0 within 15s - run stopped.' The native call reports success in the same millisecond - app.log: '[API] api_filterwheel_set_position called: device_id=sim_filterwheel_1, position=0' immediately followed by '[API] Filter wheel position set successfully' - but the Dart filterWheelStateProvider the wizard polls (flat_wizard_provider.dart:1372-1383, waiting for !isMoving && currentPosition == position) never reports the new position, so the wizard fails closed after 15 s. Crucially the wheel itself is fine: issuing the SAME position-0 command from the Equipment screen's filter-wheel card moved it and the card updated to 'L / #1' within ~5 s. So the move works everywhere except from the flat wizard, and after the wizard's two attempts the wheel was still sitting on Ha/#5. The only flat runs that ever reached the exposure stage were the ones where the wheel already happened to be at the target and the move was skipped (line 1346). Zero flats were written across four attempts: /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/flats is empty and flat_history/flat_library have 0 rows.
expected: After a successful filterWheelSetPosition the wheel state must be refreshed (event or poll) so the confirmation loop sees the new position. Failing that, the wizard must say the wheel reported success but never confirmed, and offer to proceed - not just stop.
repro: Connect Simulated Camera + Simulated Filter Wheel. Imaging -> Camera tab -> Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture -> Start Capture -> choose a folder -> Continue. Wait 15 s.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-157.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-163.png (the banner); app.log 14:57:32 and 15:01:46 (wizard commands position=0, native reports success, wheel stays on Ha); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-178.png (Equipment card still reading 'Ha / #5' twelve minutes after the wizard's second attempt) vs /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-181.png (same card reading 'L / #1' five seconds after the Equipment dropdown issued the identical position=0 at 15:14:03); sqlite3 ... 'select count(*) from flat_history' = 0 and 'find /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/flats -type f' returns nothing.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/flat_wizard_provider.dart:1370-1394 (the confirmation loop) and whatever should refresh filterWheelStateProvider after filterWheelSetPosition
proposed_fix: Re-read the wheel status from the backend inside the poll loop instead of relying solely on a pushed event, and emit a position-changed event from the filter wheel driver after a successful set.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with the wheel at Ha and the wizard asked for B. app.log 16:20:43.804816 'api_filterwheel_set_position ... position=3' immediately followed at 16:20:43.804835 by 'Filter wheel position set successfully' - and 15 s later the wizard failed closed: 'B: filter wheel did not confirm position 3 within 15s - run stopped.' with the run strip flipping to Failed (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-44.png). The asymmetry is real and I verified both directions: driving the SAME wheel from the Imaging filter chip row worked (position=4 at 16:18:47; chip row and the wizard's dropdown both then showed Ha), whereas after the wizard's move the app still believed the wheel was on Ha (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-46.png and wiz-47.png) even though the driver had accepted position 3. Root cause confirmed with its counterpart: DeviceService's changeFilter path calls _verifyFilterWheelPosition (control_helpers.dart:314-361), which polls `_backend.getFilterWheelStatus(deviceId)` and pushes the result into the provider via filterWheelNotifier.updatePosition/setMoving - while flat_wizard_provider.dart:1351-1382 calls filterWheelSetPosition directly and then polls `ref.read(filterWheelStateProvider)` with nothing in that loop ever fetching status, so it can never change. Outcome matches: zero flats written (0 files under /tmp/ns-audit/v-wizards/flats; flat_history count 0). Worse than reported: the stale state also makes the NEXT run unsafe - my second run skipped the move and exposed seven frames labelled Ha while the driver sat on position 3 (B).
